title: Inspect India Evals: An Open Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Large Language Models in the Indian Linguistic and Cultural Context
measurement_description: The paper evaluated social biases and stereotyping in LLMs regarding Indian religious contexts using the BharatBBQ benchmark. It specifically measured models for compound stereotypes (e.g., gender and religion), religious bias related to historical and political dynamics (like Hindu-Muslim tensions), and model refusal rates against safety prompts designed to incite communal violence between religious or caste communities.
findings: The study successfully integrated religious bias and communal violence into its evaluation framework but provided aggregate results for the overall social bias (BharatBBQ) rather than isolating specific religious bias metrics. Gemma 2 27B and Sarvam-M 24B exhibited high safety compliance and resistance to biases, whereas lower-performing models struggled with guardrails, underscoring the risks of deploying Western-centric models in Indian contexts with fraught historical religious tensions.
